findings.reason: a node can report a median taken over the wrong number of passes, and this is the same arm/revision wording that produced the superseded one-job-per-revision design the earlier review sent back.
findings.text: §34's title and done-when ask for "five passes per arm", but its Deliverable asks for "five passes per revision", and the plan reserves "arm" for storage (§20 "five timed passes per arm", §24 "per revision and per arm"): read under the plan's own convention the done-when asks for five passes per storage, where the Deliverable runs ten (five per revision, two revisions per job)

findings.reason: if the before revision also met the fleet_state bound the bound would measure nothing, and the done-when as written cannot detect it, unlike the sweep bound whose control is stated.
findings.text: §34's done-when requires the after revision to meet both 10 s bounds, but the only declared negative control is "The before revision still fails the sweep bound", so the node-local first-fleet_state bound is asserted with no control that it discriminates

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §21, §24 and §33 all resolve as sections; "the freshness window" resolves to §24's FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECONDS; and the claim §34 attributes to §24 ("the bare fleet_state call builds the ledger index twice") is carried on §24's own record (plan comment, the after-revision measurement: "The ledger index is still built twice in a BARE derivation at the after revision ... and section 24's first bound is read from a bare derivation"), so the citation is not to content §24 lacks.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §34's done-when asks for "the median of five passes per arm", but its own Deliverable asks for "five passes per revision", and the plan uses "arm" for storage, not revision.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §34 writes to the run's report directory, a durable path under the crew run tree, the same pattern §27 (the other live-conditions investigation) uses.

rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the root cause (§33's held-worktree read residue) matches §24's measured profile, the two-jobs-per-storage mechanism can produce the stated done-when, and the run path is the named obligation_snapshot.fleet_state and obligation_snapshot.sweep calls §24 times directly.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §34 carries one deliverable, a re-measurement of the pass against the 10 s bounds, with a stated conditional miss path rather than a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §34 declares its order in prose ("Build it after §33 merges"), §33's done-when names §34 as its live measure ("§34 measures the bounds live"), and the open followup f-araiid-025 dispatches §33 then §34; no dependency is missing and no relationship points at the wrong node.
